newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NBP weakens zloty to aid exports - c.banker.
newsitem.headline: Polish NBP weakens zloty to aid exports - c.banker.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland's deputy president said that the bank's interventions that weakened the zloty by about 0.7 percent since last Thursday aimed to help exporters and keep a cap on the trade deficit.

The central bank has bought nearly $500 million of the domestic forex market through interventions since Thursday and knocked down the zloty to 2.5 percent from the parity rate from around three percent.
"(These interventions) should support exports and act as a coolant for imports," Witold Kozinski told bankers at an annual banking association meeting.
"The central bank's exchange rate as well as interest rate policy is aimed at stabilising the trade deficit," he added.
Over the first two months of this year the current account deficit amounted to $1.1 billion, against a $1.4 billion shortfall for all of 1996.

Kozinski said there were dangers in interventions, including large inflows of money supply-boosting foreign capital into Polish debt. But he said that such a small move in the zloty exchange rate would not push up consumer prices.
"This type of policy has its dangers...but we don't think that this move, which pushed the zloty down about 0.7 percentage points, will cause prices to move," Kozinski said.
The central bank has recently increased open market operations to sterilise much of the foreign investor inflows into Polish treasuries set off by the zloty's fall last week.
The NBP has been keeping real interest rates rising and market rates high since late 1996, to cool quickly growing domestic demand along with thirst for imported consumer goods.
